title: Probe-led failover safeguard for rate and timeout triggers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a probe-led automatic fallback and circuit-safeguard mechanism that uses composite trip scoring (429 spikes, request timeouts, 5xx error rate) plus active probing to decide soft-open and hard-open circuit actions per-region and per-tier. The goal is to provide safer, more explainable automatic failovers for region selection and model variant fallback without causing cascading evictions for noisy tenants.
background: We currently rely on simple threshold-based circuit triggers (e.g., >10% 5xx over 1m) which produce noisy evictions and poor user experience for transient spikes. Recent incidents showed tenants being routed away aggressively during short-lived infra blips. We need a more nuanced system that combines passive telemetry with lightweight active probes and decaying trip scores to avoid flapping and to allow quick recovery when the target becomes healthy.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use a continuous trip score (0-100) computed from weighted signals rather than binary thresholds; weights are configurable per-region and per-tier.
Incorporate active probes before executing a full-scale failover to avoid routing away for transient anomalies; probes are small, fast requests that exercise the same model variant and path.
Soft-open: when trip score crosses warning band, move traffic progressively (10% -> 30% -> 50%) to fallback variant while continuing to probe origin and maintain telemetry.
Hard-open: when trip score >= critical threshold and probe confirms degradation, route all eligible traffic to fallback and start longer cooldown with decaying probation.
Per-tenant sensitivity: provide probation windows and lower weight for noisy tenants to prevent tenant-scoped evictions from global triggers.
Risk: Probes increase load marginally. Mitigation: probe rate is limited and scheduled adaptively (exponential backoff) and routes go through dedicated low-latency probe queue.
We avoid coupling probe success to business-critical telemetry (e.g., do not use probe tokens in billing counters) to keep cost accounting clean.
Rollout strategy will be staged: non-critical models -> low-volume tenants -> broader rollout. Feature flags will guard behavior.
False-positive risk managed by requiring both passive signal threshold AND at least 1 failed probe (or N/2 failed probes within window) before hard-open.
Trade-off: longer detection window reduces false positives but increases time-to-degrade; we provide config knobs per customer/tier to tune this.
Compatibility: must work with existing model variant mapping and smart routing policies (regional, tiered) and interact with existing autoscale signals (do not trigger autoscale by itself).
implementation_notes: Trip score components: 429 spike (30% weight), 5xx rate (30%), median latency tail (p99) above SLO (20%), timeout count (10%), probe failures (10%). Weights configurable via Console.
Scoring algorithm: exponential decay of historical evidence with half-life parameter (default 5m) to allow rapid recovery.
Active probes: small inference calls with short max-seq and 200ms timeout; probe payloads stored in probe-store; probes use dedicated probe lane with capped concurrency.
Probe scheduling: start with 1 probe/sec per troubled route, scale up to 5/sec during confirmation, back off with exponential backoff up to 10m between probe bursts.
Soft-open traffic steering: use token-based gradual split implemented in router (10% -> 30% -> 50%) with minimum observation period of 60s between steps.
Hard-open cooldown: 5m default, with decay-based probation allowing partial traffic after 50% reduction in trip score and 2 successful probes spaced 30s apart.
Public API and Console: expose trip score, component contributions, probe history, and last action (soft-open/hard-open/recovery) on per-route and per-tenant dashboards.
Telemetry: emit events: trip_score_update, probe_sent, probe_result, route_adjustment, circuit_state_change. Tag events with region, tier, model_variant, and tenant.
Testing: add unit tests for scoring math, integration tests with synthetic 429/timeouts, and chaos tests simulating regional network partitions.
Fallback variants: prefer CPU-optimized smaller quantized variants for quick failover, but allow customer policy to opt-out for quality-sensitive routes.

acceptance_criteria: Trip score algorithm matches spec and weights are configurable via Console.
Active probes execute from probe lane and do not exceed configured concurrency or rate limits.
Soft-open and hard-open transitions happen according to rules in design_decisions_and_tradeoffs and are reversible via probe success.
No user-facing errors increase by >2% for blue/green canary during staged rollout (measured via canary dashboards).
Dashboards show per-route trip score, probe history, and the last routing action; alerts fire when circuits flap >3 times in 10m.
Integration tests show correct behavior for synthetic 429 burst, timeout flood, and sustained 5xx scenarios.
Feature flag allows immediate rollback without data loss or routing inconsistency.
risks_and_mitigation: Probe overhead could add load during wide-scale incidents: limit probe rate and add global switch to disable probes under extreme load.
Mis-tuned weights may cause slow reaction or overreaction: include canary default and tooling to replay historical incidents to tune weights.
Tenant-specific noise: implement per-tenant scaling and the ability to mark tenants as 'noisy' and lower their signal contribution.
Edge-case: paired-region network partitions causing asymmetric probe results; require confirmation from at least two independent signals before hard-open for multi-region routes.
